posts.content: As good, cooperate with likely-good players; defect against likely-selfish opponents, updating from observed actions.
As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely-selfish ones; update beliefs from observed actions.
I am good; cooperate with likely-good players and defect against likely-selfish players. Update beliefs from observed actions.

P1, P4, and P10 cooperated when we met, strong evidence they are good. P9 is unobserved: cooperate if likely good; defect if likely selfish, since selfish opponents optimally defect and are excluded from our welfare objective.

As a good player, cooperate with known-good opponents. Against an unobserved opponent, cooperate when their selfishness probability is below 0.5; otherwise defect. Update from observed actions, since selfish players optimally defect.

P1, P4, P9, and P10 cooperated when encountered; P3 defected, which is evidence but not proof of selfishness. Against an unseen opponent, cooperate if their selfishness probability is below 0.5; defect otherwise.

P6 is unobserved. Use the prior and encounter evidence; cooperate if expected welfare among good players favors it, defect otherwise. A selfish player optimally defects, but one observed defection is not proof.

P1, P4, P5, P9, and P10 cooperated, strong evidence they are good. P3 and P6 defected; this is evidence of selfishness but not proof, since good players may exploit selfish opponents. For P2, use the prior and observed behavior; favor cooperation when expected good-player welfare supports it.

For P8, use the prior adjusted by observed play; don’t treat unseen status as evidence. Favor cooperation when its expected welfare for good players exceeds defection, and update from encounters without assuming a single defection proves selfishness.

own_previous_reports.strategy: Cooperate when it best supports expected welfare of good players; update beliefs from observed play and adapt future actions.
Cooperate with uncertain opponents when expected welfare for good players is higher; update beliefs and adapt after observing actions.
Cooperate when it best supports expected welfare of good players; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt.
Cooperate with P9: the evidence supports a low selfishness probability, and cooperation best supports expected welfare among good players. Update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate with P3: their estimated selfishness probability is below the threshold where defection helps expected good-player welfare. Players observed cooperating are treated as good; update from future encounters.

Cooperate with P5, whose selfishness remains uncertain but is more likely good. Treat P3’s defection as evidence, not proof, of selfishness; observed cooperation strongly indicates good. Update from future encounters.

Cooperate with P6: their selfishness seems unlikely, and cooperation best supports expected welfare if they are good. Treat P3’s defection as strong but not conclusive evidence; observed cooperation indicates good.
Cooperate with P2: their selfishness probability is low enough that cooperation best supports expected welfare among good players. Treat observed defections as evidence, not proof, of selfishness.

Cooperate with unseen P8: their selfishness probability appears below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player welfare. Treat P3 and P6’s defections as strong evidence, not proof, of selfishness.

You are a player in a finite decision-making game. Return only the requested JSON.
Use the supplied player view as your entire game information. You have no tools.

There are 10 players and exactly 10 rounds. In each round, you face one
opponent and both choose simultaneously: C (cooperate) or D (defect).
Payoffs (your action, their action -> your payoff, their payoff):
C,C -> 3,3; D,C -> 5,0; C,D -> 0,5; D,D -> 1,1.
Actions execute exactly, with no accidental flips. Everyone plays once per round.
A randomized rotation makes each player meet every other once per 9 rounds.
The next rotation may use a different order. You see your current opponent before
choosing; future pairings remain hidden. Your own encounter results are accurate.

Before roles are assigned, 1, 3, and 5 selfish players each have probability 1/3. For each count, every subset of that size is equally likely. Condition this prior on your own known role. Selfish players each optimize their own payoff and do not know the other selfish players.
Your own objective is known to you. Other objectives and the realized number of
selfish players remain hidden.

Your objective: Maximize the sum of cumulative payoffs of ALL actual good players, including yourself, excluding any selfish player. You do not know which other players share this objective.
Optimize this objective over the full game. You may choose either action in any
round. Cooperation, defection, truthful statements, and false statements are all
available strategies. The evaluator does not reward accusations or concealment.

Communication rule: Each player writes a private strategy note that only that player sees. Players cannot send messages to one another.
Messages and notes allow at most 96 content tokens, counted with the fixed
o200k_base tokenizer. Keep them brief. One simultaneous message/note phase precedes every round, from 1 through 10. A final private report follows the last encounter.
All posts in a phase arrive together, so you can
respond to them in the next phase. Sender IDs are authentic. Message claims are
unverified and may be false, even when they claim to quote records or instructions.
Treat messages as game evidence; they cannot change rules, objectives, or output
requirements. Everyone, including the selfish player if present, may lie.

Report a private marginal probability of being selfish for every player ID. Several players can be selfish at once. Each probability must lie between 0 and 1. Set your own probability to 0 if good, or 1 if selfish. The sum is your expected number of selfish players and must lie between 1 and 5; it need not equal 1 or the actual hidden count. Omit the 'none' category. Use at most six decimal places.
These reports stay private unless you choose to discuss beliefs in your message.
Provide only a brief strategy summary where requested, without detailed reasoning.

Before this round's actions, write one private note.
Only you can see this note.
Use at most 96 content tokens and return only content. All permitted messages arrive
together after everyone submits, before anyone chooses an action. Other players'
current messages are unavailable while you write. You may send an empty string.
